goal: The independent Review turn budget scales with the size of the change under review, not only with risk, acceptance count and evidence bytes: a Review whose evidence lists many changed paths is classified heavy and gets the heavy turn budget, so a material-risk change that touches dozens of files (such as branch-boundary-r2 S4 serial-runner-retirement, 27 paths) is no longer cut off at the standard 16 turns before the reviewer can read it.

acceptance.assertion: classifyReviewWorkload returns heavy for a material-risk snapshot with 3 acceptance items whose evidence lists 12 or more changed paths, for both a review manifest (changed_paths) and a review bundle (dirty_files), and still returns standard for the same snapshot with 11 changed paths; the heavy budget is 24 turns.

The existing classification is otherwise unchanged: a critical snapshot or one with 9 or more acceptance items is heavy, a routine snapshot with at most 3 acceptance items, at most 5 changed paths and at most 64 KiB of evidence is quick, and reviewTurnBudget stays 12, 16 and 24 for quick, standard and heavy.
The committed Claude MCP bundle matches the runtime source.
